description: Every finding carries a human-readable remediation string so consumers (humans and the controller's steer skill) get an actionable next step, not just a verdict.

requirements.title: Per-finding remediation text
requirements.description: Each scanner runner must attach a concrete remediation string to every finding it emits (e.g. gitleaks -> 'rotate the exposed credential and purge it from history; move it to vault'; osv/govulncheck -> 'bump <module> to >= <patched version>').

validation.notes: A gitleaks finding's remediation references rotation and vault.
An osv-scanner finding's remediation names the patched version to bump to.
No emitted finding has an empty remediation field.

requirements.title: API security header validation
requirements.description: Security Health must validate that first-party Go API surfaces centralize baseline browser security headers at the router or middleware boundary, and must flag credentialed wildcard CORS without requiring a generic CORS policy.

validation.notes: Missing centralized security headers produce an ERROR finding.
Credentialed wildcard CORS is flagged while normal CORS is not mandated.
Security Health's own API middleware stamps the required baseline headers.

requirements.title: Safe security header autofix
requirements.description: Security Health's deterministic fixer must preview and apply only low-risk generated-Go API security-header middleware edits, and must return no-op guidance for unsupported shapes instead of guessing.

validation.notes: Preview is dry-run; apply creates the middleware and registers it in the generated server shape.
Shared Fix RPC maps Security Health candidates into scenario-validation FixResponse.
CLI preview sends normalized rule ids through the shared Fix RPC.
